JUDGMENT: ( per Mr . G. Nar en d ar C.J.)

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the
learned Deputy Advocate General for the State.
2. The case of the petitioner is that M/ s Cham an Lal
Educational Trust, Roorkee, Haridwar is running three-four colleges from the sam e prem ises i.e. Chaman Lal
Degree College, Chaman Lal Law College, Cham an Lal
College of Pharmacy and the sam e is contrary to the UGC
guidelines and also the Bar Council guidelines.
3. We have queried as to whether they have
approached the com petent authorities, nam ely, the UGC

and the Bar Council of India with their com plaint, to
which, petitioner's counsel fairly subm its that they have
not m ade any effort to raise the issue with the competent
authority.
4. In that view of the m atter, we are of the opinion that
the instant writ petition is prem ature. In the event, the
petitioners are aggrieved by the actions of the
educational trust, it is always open to them to raise issue
with the com petent authority and in the event of any in-action, thereafter, approach this Court.
5. The writ petition PIL is straightaway filed seeking for
certain reliefs, maintainability of which, in our opinion, is
doubtful. In that view of the m atter, the writ petition is
disposed of by granting liberty to petitioners to make
representation to the concerned authorities. If such
representation is m ade, the competent authorities shall
consider and dispose of the same as expeditiously as
possible.
